{{short description|Danish theoretical biologist and philosopher}}
[[File:Emmeche.jpg|thumb|right|Claus Emmeche in Estonia, 2006.]]
'''Claus Emmeche''' (born 1956) is a [[Danish people|Danish]] [[theoretical biologist]] and [[philosopher]], one of founders of contemporary [[biosemiotics]].<ref>Favareau, D. 2008. [https://www.academia.edu/20369648/The_IASS_Roundtable_discussion_on_biosemiotics_A_discussion_with_some_founders_of_the_field The IASS roundtable on biosemiotics: A discussion with some founders of the field]. ''The American Journal of Semiotics'' 24(1/3): 1–21.</ref><ref>Favareau, D. (ed.) 2010. ''Essential Readings in Biosemiotics''. Springer, p. 629.</ref> He is associate professor at the [[University of Copenhagen]], and is head of the Center for the Philosophy of Nature and Science Studies at the Faculty of Science (CPNSS, hosted by the [[Niels Bohr Institute]]).

His research interests are in [[philosophy of science]], especially philosophy of biology, [[theoretical biology]] (especially [[morphogenesis]] and [[evolution]], developmental systems, [[complex systems]]), [[artificial life]], [[biosemiotics]], and other areas within [[philosophy]]. He has made pioneering studies in the field of semiotics of [[friendship]].

==Activism==
Claus Emmeche was one of the organizers of a petition directed at [[Helge Sander]]'s education reforms, which the petition claimed undermined [[academic freedom]] by granting a broad majority of the management of universities to people from outside the academic community. As of August, 2008, 35% of Danish academics had signed the petition.<ref>[http://www.universityworldnews.com/article.php?story=20080828144406821&mode=print Ard Jongsma, "Denmark: Academics sign up to protest", ''University World News'', No. 0042, 31 Aug. 2008.]</ref>  By November, this had risen to about 50%.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.dm.dk/NyhederOgDebat/Nyhedsarkiv/2008/November/6488Underskrifter.aspx | title=6488 Underskrifter For En Ny Universitetslov Overdraget | date=November 21, 2008 | accessdate=2008-12-23 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101230134844/http://www.dm.dk/NyhederOgDebat/Nyhedsarkiv/2008/November/6488Underskrifter.aspx | archive-date=December 30, 2010 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

* ''The Garden in the Machine: The Emerging Science of Artificial Life'', Princeton University Press, ({{ISBN|0691029032}})<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sigmund |first=Karl |date=1994-09-23 |title=Virtually A-Life: The Garden in the Machine. Translated from the Danish edition (1991) by Steven Sampson. |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.265.5180.1900.b |journal=Science |volume=265 |issue=5180 |pages=1900–1901 |doi=10.1126/science.265.5180.1900.b|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ekstig |first=Borje |date=March 1995 |title=The Garden in the Machine: The Emerging Science of Artificial Life. Princeton, NJ: Princeton University Press, 1994 |url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/092137409500700206 |journal=Cultural Dynamics |language=en |volume=7 |issue=2 |pages=265–269 |doi=10.1177/092137409500700206 |issn=0921-3740|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Van Dyke Parunak |first=H. |date=July 1995 |title=Book review: The Garden in the Machine: The Emerging Science of Artificial Life by Claus Emmeche (Princeton University Press, 1994) |url=https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/208628.1065828 |journal=ACM SIGART Bulletin |language=en |volume=6 |issue=3 |pages=15–16 |doi=10.1145/208628.1065828 |issn=0163-5719|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* ''Downward Causation: Minds, Bodies and Matter'' by Peter Bogh Andersen, Claus Emmeche, Niels Ole Finnemann, and Peder Voetmann Christiansen.  Princeton University Press, ({{ISBN|0691029032}}) (1996)

London: Imperial College Press. (2011) [https://web.archive.org/web/20120415052620/http://www.icpress.co.uk/lifesci/p771.html See]

In Danish, Emmeche has authored or co-authored at least 5 books, 25 articles, and over 47 other works.
